summary: A 60-foot brick tower of 1838 at the north end of Little Cumberland Island, Georgia; dark since 1915 and now owned by a private island association.

lens.where: taken down by the keeper in 1862 (Du Pont letter); later location not recorded in the sources

access.note: Owned by the Little Cumberland Island Association; access restricted to homeowners and their guests (LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Oil run out of the casks by an intruder with false keys (LighthouseFriends); keeper recovered 47 gallons
Pilotage of the slave ship Wanderer through St. Andrew Sound (accounts differ)
Keeper took down the lens and kept it from the Confederacy (accounts differ)
Light back in operation 1 September 1867 with a third-order lens
Brick retaining wall built around the tower
Keeper Robertson commended for efforts to save an abandoned boathouse from fire
Tug Rambler wrecked off the station on 5 January 1915
Light dimmed 15 March 1915 after decommissioning in 1913
Tower and six acres sold at auction to R. L. Phillips Company for $800
Little Cumberland Island Association buys the island
Association restores the tower; spiral stair replaced; jalousie windows installed

wrecks.outcome: Brunswick News, 7 Feb 1915: four men and two deck hands lost their lives; the two deck hands' bodies were found on Little Cumberland a day after the wreck; a body found on Cumberland beach on Friday (5 Feb) was identified on 9 Feb as one of the crew. LighthouseFriends: four men aboard, all lost, one body recovered. The two accounts differ on the number lost.

corrections.why: The nomination gives the fixed light as 78 feet above sea level (23.8 m). The record's 22.0 m is not supported by the sources read.
The nomination gives the range as 14 1/2 nautical miles.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination calls James Clubb the keeper who guided the Wanderer on 29 November 1858. LighthouseFriends says he became keeper the following year, and the archive roster begins his stint in 1859. The marker calls him a pilot, not the keeper.

The nomination and LighthouseFriends give 29 November 1858 for the pilotage (LighthouseFriends also gives the arrival at Jekyll Island as 29 November). The Georgia Encyclopedia gives 28 November for the arrival at Jekyll Island; the marker gives 28 November for the Wanderer's arrival off the Georgia coast.

notes_for_editor: Sources read: the NRHP nomination (1989; Sections 7 and 8, cited by section because the continuation sheets have no printed page numbers); LighthouseFriends (facts only, paraphrased and cited); the USLHS place record and roster (cached; roster matched by name and position, 0.66 km); Light-House Board 1896-97 (printed p. 100, scan p. 118, entry 702, checked on the page image); Commissioner fiscal 1915 (printed p. 62, scan p. 67, checked on the page image: the row reads 'J. Robertson, keeper, and M. B. Wilder, assistant keeper' against 'Parties searching bodies of crew of Rambler, wrecked near station' and 'Gave shelter and otherwise assisted searching parties'; the OCR drops the middle of the nature-of-assistance line, so the story paraphrases it); Bulletin 1912 (printed and PDF p. 48, checked on the page image: 'John Robertson, keeper of Little Cumberland Island Light Station, Ga., has been commended for his efforts in endeavoring to save an abandoned boathouse from fire'); Bulletin 1937 (printed p. 77, PDF p. 33, checked on the page image: 'discontinued over 20 years ago'); Brunswick News, 7 and 9 February 1915, page 1 (Chronicling America OCR); Georgia Encyclopedia and the Jekyll Island marker for the Wanderer. The Wanderer is told only from secondary sources and the nomination: no primary record of the pilotage was read, so the story gives the accounts side by side. OCR CAUTION: the 1896-97 report's OCR reads 186 feet of picket fence for the new boathouse entry; the page image reads 185. The story follows the image; the evidence quote avoids the number. DISAGREEMENTS LEFT FOR THE EDITOR: (1) Rambler deaths: the Brunswick News counts four men and two deck hands (six) lost; LighthouseFriends counts four men aboard, all lost, one body recovered. (2) Tower height: 60 feet (nomination) vs 61 feet (LighthouseFriends); the record's 22.0 m focal height is corrected from the nomination's 78 feet above sea level (23.8 m). (3) The Clubb keepership in November 1858: the nomination calls him keeper, the roster starts his stint in 1859. (4) Wanderer arrival date: 28 November (encyclopedia, marker) vs 29 November (nomination, LighthouseFriends, for the pilotage). The archive's roster and LighthouseFriends disagree on some end years (for example Bruggeman 1901-1905 vs 1901-1906; Thelning 1903-1906 vs 1903-1905); the roster's years are used. Horatio Harris (marker) is not on the archive roster for this station and is not listed as a keeper. The record's 22.0 m focal height and 14.0 nm range are corrected from the nomination; the 'characteristic' is left out of facts because no source read gives one. Accessed dates use the session date (2026-10-27); the workflow message gives 2026-10-22, and the accessed dates were not changed. Confidence is medium: the 1838-1915 physical history is well sourced, but the Wanderer and the 1915 wreck rest on accounts that differ.
